variants.headline: Looking back: a company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen a company fail.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A company had gone under in {colony}.

A failed company is not a complete statement of creditor recoveries or wider commercial conditions. Owners and managers should distinguish the individual event from an economy-wide conclusion. A sound assessment requires the firm's actual position, rather than an assumed trade, a guessed debt or a forecast attached to failure alone.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We judge {target} critically. Business failure deserves more than a shrug, and the standards of stewardship should be examined rather than dismissed as irrelevant once an enterprise has gone under.
